# Domainry Builder V1

Drive every development batch through:

```text
requirements → domain facts → calculation ownership/persistence/correction → capability discovery → model → apply → verify → done
```

Platform capabilities determine the implementation mapping; they never determine the business facts. Do not start from Dataset, Report, metadata, an Action shape, or another Runtime feature and work backward into a domain model. Settle occurred facts, summaries, simulations, calculation ownership, persistence, and correction before capability discovery. Only two or more unresolved, mutually incompatible choices that change an explicitly required observable business result, authorization allow/deny result, amount/unit semantics, irreversible external effect, or business-state flow form a product business ambiguity; block only the smallest affected modeling slice. Missing optional metadata, preferences, and reversible mechanisms are not product blockers. Contract discovery and reversible technical defaults are not substitutes for business facts.

The frontend under `frontend/**` is evidence of product demand, not automatically a complete business specification. Inspect routes, screens, typed API contracts, Mock adapters, tests, roles, states, and copy read-only while settling requirements and domain truth; never promote Mock behavior into business truth. This Skill never creates, modifies, or deletes `frontend/**`. Route each mismatch to the owner proved by the explicit requirement, published Runtime contract, typed frontend API, Mock/tests, and real behavior. A frontend- or Mock-owned mismatch is a finding for owner `frontend`, never a backend workaround or frontend edit.

## Route exactly once

Choose one route before loading supporting resources. Do not combine the routes.

### Whole-project development

For every normal requirements, build, repair, integration, acceptance, or whole-project continuation batch, read [development-guide.md](references/development-guide.md) **completely before starting** and use it as the only execution workflow. It contains the authoritative TODO/Gate process, full normal-development CLI map, project boundaries, phase rules, required reference routing, Runtime acceptance, and terminal policy. Follow every applicable routed reference it requires. A full batch reads the whole guide; a light batch may omit only TODO sections under the guide's explicit light-batch rules, never guide loading or an applicable authority.

The routing map below is a reachability contract, not permission to read only selected guide sections:

| Moved entrypoint section / contract | Whole-project authority |
| --- | --- |
| workflow, routing, and batch scale | [whole-project workflow](references/development-guide.md#whole-project-workflow) |
| loaded Skill, CLI identity, and normal command surface | [CLI identity and canonical command map](references/development-guide.md#cli-identity-and-canonical-command-map) |

### Explicit source-finalization continuation

Use this route only when the caller explicitly requests `source-finalization-continuation`, accepts and freezes upstream requirements/modeling, confirms the current source-finalization checkpoint remains valid, and limits scope exactly to:

```text
valid Actions project check → source finalize → module-focused Go test
```

Run the loaded Skill's resolver once with an explicit project-relative focused package:

```sh
"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-context.py" \
  --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" \
  --profile source-finalization-continuation \
  --focused-test-package <project-relative-./package>
```

The returned `continuation` envelope atomically owns this session's three-Gate TODO, synchronized Gate IDs, current checkpoint identity, and exact `run_recipes`. Execute those recipes in order and use no other workflow. Do **not** read `references/development-guide.md`, `assets/DEVELOPMENT_TODO.template.md`, or any whole-project reference for this profile.

This route is caller authorization, never inferred from project state. Missing, stale, unsafe, or ambiguous session/checkpoint/CLI identity, a package outside the project, a missing focused package, or a conflicting/partial session TODO fails closed. Do not repair such a conflict by deleting or rewriting managed state. The compact route does not bypass the Host's complete loading of this `SKILL.md` and does not change whole-project behavior.

## Loaded Skill and CLI identity

Resolve `SKILL_ROOT` from the exact filesystem path of the `SKILL.md` loaded for this task. Every Builder command, resolver, Gate runner, template, and reference must come from that same root. The package has one executable: `"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-cli"` (`domainry-cli.exe` on Windows). Never discover it through `PATH`, substitute another installed Skill's binary, call Domainry Plane directly, or invent a neighboring command.

For whole-project work, the guide requires the default resolver once at task start and binds `DOMAINRY_CLI`, the Host session ID, TODO, compact resume packet, one-time authoring context, and package identity to its result. Run `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" version --json` before every other Builder command. Re-run the resolver only if the exact project root or Host session identity changes. For the explicit continuation, the compact resolver call above supplies and validates the same package CLI identity without loading whole-project context.

## Universal safety and evidence invariants

- Treat Runtime-owned identifiers, hierarchy values, principal claims, cursors, and other canonical representations as opaque. Resolve them through the published typed client, `GET /identity/principal-context`, a formal seed/admin path, or a persisted Runtime result and carry them unchanged. Never construct, trim, pad, normalize, inject, or query Runtime-owned persistence to discover them. A missing formal source blocks the affected journey.
- Keep project-owned authoring in `backend/model/*.json`, referenced `backend/reports/*.sql`, project-owned backend source/tests, and the current session's `.domainry/development/<agent-session-id>.md`. Never hand-edit generated source, frozen contracts, Runtime manifests, receipts, audits, caches, journals, managed Runtime state, or other CLI-owned `.domainry/**` delivery state. Never create symlinks, traversal paths, special files, placeholders, empty success handlers, or business source that ignores its generated capabilities.
- `model apply` is the only normal-development release command. Its reviewed `--product-surfaces` value is an integration boundary, never frontend mutation authorization. Repair reported model/input failures and rerun the same command; never split publication/materialization or bypass destructive/evolution review.
- Every check, finalize, and focused-test command must run through its own Gate on its first real execution. Never run it directly first, rerun merely to obtain evidence, search historical receipts, or attach another command's receipt. A receipt proves only its original Gate and current bound identities; changed bound source/model/Runtime/artifact content makes it stale.
- Before model authoring, bind every acceptance journey to its requirement, formal actor/session/principal, canonical context and identifiers, isolated setup, command/read surfaces, non-empty positive oracle, exact denied/conflict and unchanged-state oracle, durable effect, and dependencies. Do not create a second plan. Scope-sensitive journeys use same-record contrasts through real Runtime sessions; arbitrary errors, empty results, and residue from another case do not prove success. For unchanged/replay record hashes, use `runtimeRecordDurableSnapshot` (or copied-harness `durable_record_snapshot`), never the whole HTTP response body.
- After current source finalization and focused tests pass, run one highest-risk semantic canary across formal identity/context resolution → command → persisted effect → actor-visible read-back before broad Runtime integration. A canary failure blocks dependents and is repaired once at its owner; it never shrinks the frozen model or acceptance denominator.
- Never claim above current evidence. Structural verification/package success cannot establish real-data scenario acceptance. Completion requires the applicable evidence Gate, an empty finding inventory, the guide's terminal policy, and the TODO consistency check; unresolved product prerequisites are implementation/Foundation defects, not cosmetic limitations.

Startup fills only a missing credential; it never overwrites an existing password hash, clears a lock, or undoes a changed password. The canonical system identity is user ID `admin`, login `admin@example.com`, Admin Console `/admin`, Surface `admin_console`. In a managed development Runtime started by this workflow, a deployment without `AUTH_DEFAULT_PASSWORD` seeds every missing credential — `admin` and project-declared acceptance identities — with development default `Domainry@2026`, marked `must_change_password:true`; production rejects this value. Establish a managed-development acceptance session by logging in with that default, completing forced change through `POST /auth/change-password` with `Idempotency-Key`, and keeping the new credential only in authorized secret handoff. Never print credentials into evidence or guess passwords: five failed logins produce `auth.account_locked`, and expiry does not lift the lock; an admin session must call `POST /identity/users/{userID}/unlock`. Formal Identity API users instead use their one-time no-store password. Business Workspace and Consumer Portal actors come from project-declared non-human acceptance identities. Authentication mode, session refresh, and authorization are independent of Surface; protected operations still enforce functional permission, ownership, Action policy, assurance, and data scope.

# Project development guide Drive every development batch with one visible project document: ```text /.domainry/development/.md ``` The complete frontend under `frontend/**` provides concrete demand evidence through routes, screens, typed APIs, Mock adapters, tests, states, and copy. It may omit business rules or encode provisional assumptions, so inspect it read-only while extracting requirements and domain truth. Domainry Plane exposes backend capability contracts plus the transport-only `@domainry/runtime-client` the frontend consumes; Runtime machine contracts remain authoritative for data, authorization, navigation, and operation semantics. Frontend source stays read-only throughout the task; the recorded scope and evidence-based defect routing below turn frontend-owned defects into findings, never edits. See [runtime-client.md](runtime-client.md) for the client contract the frontend binds against. The fixed stage order is: requirements → domain facts → calculation ownership/persistence/correction → capability discovery → model → apply → verify → done. Requirements and domain facts always precede Runtime capability selection; platform shape never supplies business truth. ## Batch scale First record `Execution scope: requirements_only` or `implementation`. Use `requirements_only` only when the user requests analysis, requirements, or domain design and explicitly excludes development. It keeps the header, requirements, domain-truth design, and done sections; omit model, apply, Runtime, and verify sections with that reason in the header. Its `done` proves only the accepted requirements/domain artifact and must report no delivery or L1-L5 implementation claim. Any build, repair, integration, or end-to-end request is `implementation` and follows the normal full/light rules below. Classify every batch as `full` or `light` and record the classification with its justification in the TODO header. A light batch is an existing-project increment with no new Object, Action, role, permission, scope, or menu change; everything else is a full batch. In a light batch, instantiate the TODO with only the sections the batch touches: always keep the header, the execution rules, and the `verify` and `done` stages; under `model` and `apply`, copy only the touched subsections and record every omitted subsection in the header `Sections omitted` field with what the batch does not change and the prior accepted evidence reference. When the batch changes no Action, role, permission, scope, or menu, the entire authorization and navigation acceptance section is omitted this way. Inside a copied section, a checkbox whose subject the batch does not touch may still be closed as not applicable with the same scope evidence; a subject the batch touches is never omitted or closed as not applicable. If work discovered mid-batch breaks any light criterion, reclassify the batch as full in the TODO and complete the full-track items before proceeding. A full batch follows every stage without merging. The caller-explicit `source-finalization-continuation` route is selected and initialized from the loaded entrypoint before any whole-project resource is read. It never loads this guide, the TODO template, or another whole-project reference; its compact Gate-owned envelope is its complete workflow. For every normal whole-project session, use the following initialization unchanged. At the start of an Agent session: 1. Resolve `SKILL_ROOT` from the exact loaded `SKILL.md` path and run `"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-context.py" --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"` once. 2. Bind `DOMAINRY_CLI`, the Agent session/thread ID, and the TODO path to the resolver's returned `cli`, `session_id`, and `todo`; retain its machine-readable `authoring_context` and compact `resume_packet` across context compaction instead of repeating broad capability/schema/reference discovery. Require that CLI to be the package's single `domainry-cli` binary and verify it with `version --json`. 3. Resolve the session ID from the resolver. Its primary sources are `DOMAINRY_AGENT_SESSION_ID` in Domainry, `CODEX_THREAD_ID` in Codex, or an equivalent explicit Host value; the temporary Domainry fallback is the unique active log session whose `cwd` equals the exact project root. Treat the ID as an opaque safe filename segment. Never generate a replacement UUID, select the globally newest log session, accept an ambiguous project match, guess, shorten, borrow, or reuse another session's ID. 4. If `.domainry/development/.md` already exists, resume it because it belongs to the same session. 5. Otherwise create that exact file from `assets/DEVELOPMENT_TODO.template.md`. 6. Record the exact session ID, batch goal, original requirement, project mode, execution scope, scope, one `Frontend mutation scope`, and `requirements` as the initial current stage before implementation. 7. Add concrete project tasks beneath the template items. Do not keep a second execution plan. 8. Run `"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-gates.py" --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --session-id "$SESSION_ID" sync` once. Execute the TODO strictly top-to-bottom per the template's execution rules; never check later work merely because it happened out of order. Close checkboxes through the evidence Gate's `run`, `attach`, or explicit `mark --status not_applicable` commands, not by writing success prose. Before leaving a stage, require `status --stage --require-complete`. 9. At completion, close every item and finding, set `Current stage: done`, and run `"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-todo-check.py" --todo "$TODO_PATH"` once immediately before the final response. Repair every reported inconsistency and rerun the checker until it passes. For `requirements_only`, the formal Gate identity is the deterministic requirements-evidence closure exposed as `requirements`: the mandatory non-empty `docs/backend-requirements-prd.md`; root `requirements.md` when it exists; and, when `frontend/src/**` contains a regular source file, the complete regular-file evidence under `frontend/**` after excluding dependency, build, coverage, cache, database, log, backup, and temporary artifacts. Paths and content hashes are sorted and framed, so creation order, timestamps, worktree location, backend files, unrelated root files, and derived frontend files do not affect the identity; symlinks fail closed. A frontend-led or immutable external-reference PRD is valid without root `requirements.md`: the PRD records its authority and immutable frontend snapshot/commit or external citation, and the local frontend closure is bound automatically when present. Do not silently place another mutable local authority elsewhere; make it the canonical root `requirements.md` or incorporate its accepted facts and immutable reference identity in the PRD. Do not guess `--bind source` when no project source exists. After obtaining the Gate ID from `list`, invoke the same Gate runner with `attach --gate-id --status passed --evidence-type source_artifact --evidence-path docs/backend-requirements-prd.md --bind requirements`, or execute an applicable validator once with `run --gate-id --bind requirements -- `. Missing or empty PRD makes the binding unavailable. The requirements-only terminal “all in-scope requirements” Gate uses this closure and does not demand an implementation-coverage receipt; a change to any included evidence makes it stale. Every validation argv must itself fail closed: use no pipeline, or place `set -o pipefail`/`set -euo pipefail` inside the executed shell script before any pipeline; `tee` never turns an internal failure into a passing Gate. One Agent session corresponds to one TODO document and owns only `.domainry/development/.md`; never overwrite or update another session's document. A new session creates a new file even for related work and may reference prior session TODOs only as read-only handoff context. The TODO is the only progress ledger. Do not keep a second execution plan. Append validation findings to this document, finish the reachable round, batch repairs, and revalidate until the finding inventory is empty. One artifact may support several items, but every Gate binds the artifact and exact fact proved. Changed evidence content or a bound source, requirements artifact, model/Blueprint, Runtime manifest, identity, or receipt-named artifact makes the Gate stale and requires current evidence. Keep evidence concise and link to large artifacts instead of pasting logs. The lightweight TODO checker only detects document consistency; it runs no build or Runtime work and is not a second completion authority, evidence database, or source-wide staleness system. Keep `assets/DEVELOPMENT_TODO.template.md` in the same dependency order as this guide; if the template order is wrong, correct and validate the template before using or releasing that Skill version — never work around a misordered template by executing later sections first. ## Round discipline For every validation round: 1. Run every safely reachable check in the current stage. 2. Record the complete finding inventory in the TODO with `open` or `resolved` state and concrete evidence. 3. Group findings by shared root cause and module. 4. Repair the complete batch. 5. Re-run affected focused checks, then only the stage checks invalidated by the repair. 6. Repeat until no open finding remains. Stop early only when continuation is impossible, risks data loss or security, corrupts protected state, or invalidates the remaining results. A recoverable failure is not a reason to stop the round. ## Semantic execution contract and canary Before model authoring, close one semantic execution row for every acceptance journey in the existing backend PRD; reference those rows from the session TODO instead of creating a second plan. Each row binds: - the requirement and actor to a project-provisioned Runtime identity and formal session/principal source; - every Runtime-owned context fact or canonical identifier to the typed client, formal seed/admin path, or persisted Runtime response that supplies it; - fresh setup identities/records and any explicit dependency on another journey; - the command surface and the actor-visible read surface; - a positive oracle naming the target identity and required non-empty facts; - the exact denial, concealment, validation, or conflict status/error category plus unchanged-state oracle; - the durable database effect, replay/restart requirement, and authoritative reconciliation source. Runtime-owned identities, hierarchy values, paths, claims, cursors, and fingerprints are opaque values. Carry the formal returned value unchanged across metadata, seed data, Handler inputs, persisted records, and acceptance. Do not synthesize them from display names or conventions, and do not trim, append, case-fold, or otherwise normalize them unless the published Runtime contract explicitly owns that transformation. A missing formal source is a blocking Foundation/Runtime gap, not permission to inject a request claim or guess a representation. For each scope-sensitive row, prepare one target record and probe it through real sessions with otherwise equivalent requests: the matching actor observes that exact record and a non-empty expected result; the non-matching actor receives the contractually specified concealment/denial and produces no durable effect; when a broader application role is in scope, it observes the same record. A success status with an empty collection, null result, zero aggregate, or wrong target is a failure unless the confirmed requirement calls for that exact value. A negative probe passes only on its intended stable status/error category and unchanged state, never on an arbitrary `4xx`, `not found`, or setup failure. Choose one highest-risk row as the semantic canary, favoring a journey that crosses the most of identity/context resolution, data scope, project Action, multi-record persistence, actor-visible projection, and restart/replay. After the full model is applied, source is finalized, and focused tests pass, execute that row before the broad Runtime integration round. If it fails, mark every dependent journey blocked by that root cause, finish the reachable failure inventory, repair the owner once, and rerun the canary plus only invalidated checks. Do not spend a full acceptance round rediscovering the same upstream mismatch, but never use the canary to shrink the complete model or final denominator. ## Project and frontend boundaries The canonical project-owned authoring surfaces are: ```text backend/model/*.json declarative backend metadata inventory backend/reports/*.sql project-owned Report SQL referenced by model sql_file backend/ project-owned Go source and tests plus generated platform source .domainry/development/.md current session TODO .domainry/ CLI-managed delivery, contracts, receipts, artifacts, Runtime, and evidence ``` Git owns project-source development, so normal editors, patches, formatters, dependency tools, and Git worktrees may modify project-owned source. `.domainry/development/*.md` is the project-owned coordination exception under `.domainry/**`, with each file owned only by its matching Host session. Never hand-edit generated source; frozen Project Contracts; Runtime manifests; materialization, finalization, verification, or package receipts; audits, caches, journals, managed Runtime state, or other CLI-owned delivery state. Do not create symlinks, traversal paths, special files, placeholders, empty success handlers, or business source that never uses its generated capability set. Record exactly one `Frontend mutation scope` in the TODO header: - `integration_authorized`: the user requested a build, fix-all repair, integration, or end-to-end acceptance without narrowing the task to backend-only, and repository evidence confirms project ownership; - `backend_only`: the user explicitly limited work to backend; - `externally_owned`: another tool or owner delivered the frontend; - `unauthorized`: no current request authorizes frontend mutation. The scope records authorization context only and never changes this Skill's edit boundary: `frontend/**` remains read-only in every scope throughout the task. During integration compare the requirement, typed frontend API, published Runtime contract, Mock/tests, and real response before assigning ownership. Repair a backend or Runtime gap at its owner; never hide it behind a compatibility adapter, raw HTTP, fabricated fallback, altered Mock, or weakened test. Record a frontend- or Mock-owned defect as a finding with owner `frontend`, minimal reproduction, and contract basis. If it blocks a backend journey, mark that journey blocked without relabeling the defect as a platform gap. End-to-end acceptance here means backend end-to-end through real managed-Runtime HTTP/SSE/worker/database behavior bound to the TODO and Gate source identity. Browser-layer UI verification is outside this Skill's acceptance scope. ## New and existing projects For a new project: - Before any project-mutating `domainry-cli` command, require the exact project root to be one initialized Git worktree. If the new root is not inside another worktree, run `git init --initial-branch=main ` once and verify `git -C rev-parse --show-toplevel` equals the exact root. Never retry mutations before this check, initialize an existing project without authorization, or create a nested repository inside another worktree. - Preserve the full requirement; do not silently reduce it to an MVP, demo, phase, or core subset. - Establish users, roles, goals, lifecycles, exceptional paths, and the complete operation inventory before modeling. - Apply industry business practices where they clarify the requested product without expanding its scope. - Before first backend publication, model local/test-only non-human acceptance identities, their formal login/session path, required Workforce profiles and assignments, departments/jobs/positions, business menu definitions, role-menu assignments, and the minimum real records for every acceptance journey. The implementer may add the minimum contrasting identities needed to prove same-record allow/deny, data-Scope, and requester isolation; these are acceptance fixtures, not evidence of the product's organization size or role cardinality. Do not defer these prerequisites to verify or seed online credentials. For an existing project: - Read current requirement documents, Git state, backend source, metadata, tests, and managed delivery state. - Record current behavior and the affected dependency closure in the TODO. - Plan only the requested increment and required regression coverage. - Retain valid existing source; do not rewrite it to manufacture workflow evidence. ## Initialization Resolve `SKILL_ROOT` from the exact loaded `SKILL.md` path and run `"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-context.py" --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"` once at task start. Do not move, copy, merge, or recreate the managed root by hand. ## requirements ### Produce the backend dependency PRD For a new project or a complete frontend Mock-to-Runtime replacement, create or update `docs/backend-requirements-prd.md` from `assets/BACKEND_REQUIREMENTS_PRD.template.md`. This is not a marketing PRD or a pixel inventory: it is the accepted demand contract for what Runtime and project metadata/source must provide. For a light existing-project increment, record an equivalent traceable PRD delta in the current session TODO or update the accepted backend PRD, and reference the unchanged baseline. **Reference mode for structured input.** A source is structured when its rules live in stable titled/numbered sections citable as ` §N`. Test per requirement: if one section states the rule completely, cite it — do not restate it; rewrite only what must be assembled from scattered evidence (Mock adapters, tests, verbal decisions, multiple documents). A reference-mode PRD carries requirement IDs, classifications, owner/capability mapping, decisions, acceptance criteria, and the matrices, each row citing its source section; restating an already-structured source is prohibited waste. Both modes keep the Resolve-critical-ambiguity table and full traceability. Read frontend evidence in this order: route/page registry and user journeys; typed application API; Mock adapters/fixtures; state stores and hooks; form/list/detail/report components; permission/menu guards; tests and stories; visible copy. Also read the current explicit requirement and latest accepted product/design documents. Legacy APIs or prior backends are `legacy_reference` until the current requirement or frontend confirms them. This inspection is read-only even when later integration is authorized to repair frontend source. A Mock fixture, adapter behavior, test expectation, or visible affordance proves demand or a current assumption; it does not establish a business rule without higher-precedence evidence. Use this precedence when evidence conflicts: 1. explicit current user decision; 2. latest accepted requirement or design contract; 3. latest implemented frontend behavior; 4. typed API and Mock semantics; 5. frontend tests; 6. legacy/reference implementation. Do not erase conflicts using precedence alone. Record the conflict, affected requirement IDs, selected authority, and confirmation evidence. Classify every item as `confirmed`, `recommended`, `open`, `frontend_only`, or `legacy_reference`. Extract at least: - pages, routes, entry conditions, actors, journeys, and observable success; - canonical object identities, fields, relations, list/detail/form/report shapes, filters, search, sort, and pagination; - commands, outcomes, bulk operations, state transitions, approvals, cancellation/correction paths, and durable side effects; - roles, permissions, record scope, sensitive fields, menu visibility, and allow/deny behavior; - observable validation, conflict, retry, and replay behavior; discover Runtime-owned stable error categories/codes and choose concurrency/idempotency mechanisms after the business invariant is settled; - calculations with inputs, units, formula, policy/version date, rounding point/mode, examples, and refund/correction behavior; - schedulers, automations, notifications, connectors, files, audit, outbox, and external effects; - presentation-only behavior that remains `frontend_only` and must not create backend metadata. Build a traceability matrix with one row per requirement: `frontend evidence → requirement ID → Runtime owner/capability → model resource or approved source gap → permission/data scope → acceptance journey`. Where the frontend exposes a typed API, count its backend-bound operations and account for every one in the matrix as implemented, platform-reused, frontend-only, superseded, or open. Every route must map to a journey or an explicit frontend-only disposition. Every write operation must name authorization, observable validation/error behavior, transaction boundary, idempotency/retry policy, durable result, and acceptance proof; Runtime-owned codes and mechanism details may point to their contract-discovery or implementation-decision row. Matrix and contract-table cells are phrases, not sentences. Once a fact is in a table (or cited by section), do not restate it in prose; prose is only for what no table column captures. ### Resolve critical ambiguity Classify every unresolved choice in the PRD before capability selection. This is the authoritative requirements-only routing rule. An item is a `business_blocker` only when accepted evidence leaves at least two concrete, mutually incompatible choices and choosing among them changes a requirement's explicitly demanded observable business result, authorization allow/deny result, amount/unit semantics, irreversible external effect, or business-state flow. A missing optional field, metadata value, preference, or mechanism is not a blocker when one deterministic conservative fallback preserves the stated core behavior. Apply the blocker only to the smallest affected requirement/model slice; never block an entire Object, Report, export, or Workflow because one optional field or later preference is open. | Decision class | Boundary | Required handling | Blocks model? | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `business_blocker` | Two or more concrete, mutually incompatible choices remain, and selecting one changes an explicitly required observable business result, authorization allow/deny result, amount/unit semantics, irreversible external effect, or business-state flow | Name the incompatible choices and the exact affected requirement/model items. Do not infer the choice from UI, fixtures, labels, legacy behavior, or implementation convenience; obtain a current user decision or accepted requirement evidence. | Yes, only for the smallest affected slice. | | `contract_discovery` | Runtime-owned formal error code/category, canonical identifier or principal/context source, or the mapping of accepted facts to Action, Workflow, metadata, or another published capability | Discover it through the typed client, fixed capability categories, or another formal Runtime contract. If the formal contract is absent, record a Foundation/Runtime owner gap; do not turn it into a product question or invent a representation. | No. It may block affected implementation or acceptance after discovery fails, but not settled business modeling. | | `safe_implementation_decision` | A purely technical, reversible choice that preserves the accepted business invariant, including stable ordering with a unique tie-breaker, pagination maximum, index, internal resource key, and audit, idempotency, or concurrency mechanism | Use the published platform standard; otherwise record one deterministic, conservative safe default with its rationale and evolution path. | No. | | `product_follow_up` | A product preference whose currently documented fallback does not change required observable results, permission, amount meaning, or business state in the accepted scope | Record the assumption, owner, fallback, excluded acceptance scope, and review trigger. Never relabel it `confirmed`. | No. | Security and privacy omissions use a conservative `safe_implementation_decision`: least privilege, sensitive by default, and no export by default, with the evolvable assumption recorded. If an explicit requirement demands export or broader disclosure of a sensitive fact, that conflict is a `business_blocker` until its authorization and disclosure boundary is confirmed. Use these nonblocking defaults without inventing product rules: - If exact decimal representation, a comparison threshold, or summation is explicit, absent currency, unit, or numeric range metadata does not block the decimal field, comparison, or aggregation. Keep optional metadata nullable and enforce only stated command preconditions. Block only the smallest comparison/conversion slice when two incompatible units are actually possible and the required result depends on choosing or converting between them. - If an asynchronous approval task and its approved/rejected outcomes are explicit but the host lifecycle has no pending state, put pending state on an independent approval Object and leave the host unchanged until the terminal effect. Missing edit/cancel/resubmit behavior is a `product_follow_up`; use conservative concurrency/idempotency that grants no extra authority and produces no duplicate effect. - If a resource is explicitly non-updatable/non-deletable but no business-role read is required, model the resource and immutable deny rules without inventing a read actor. Prove creation through a formal admin/seed path or persistence evidence; do not fabricate business read permission for acceptance. - If weekday/morning scheduling intent is explicit but timezone or holiday-calendar preference is absent, use the platform/deployment-configured deterministic timezone and a standard weekday cron, then record the preference as `product_follow_up`. Block only when the requirement explicitly demands different multi-timezone or statutory-holiday outcomes and choosing the calendar changes that required result. Only `business_blocker` blocks model authoring. Unspecified additional metadata, preferences, and reversible mechanisms do not block already settled core behavior. A contract-discovery item or safe implementation decision can still fail its later implementation, security, or acceptance Gate; the classification changes who decides the fact, never the required proof or quality bar. ## domain truth design Read [domain-truth-and-settlement.md](domain-truth-and-settlement.md) completely. Freeze the domain facts before asking what Runtime can implement; close every calculation's ownership/persistence/correction decisions per that document. A capability is an implementation option after these facts exist; it is not evidence for choosing them. Financial, payroll, points, inventory-cost, and settlement facts must remain reproducible after Settings change. If an event locks a result, model the write-side atomic Action and immutable snapshot/ledger before its Reports. Keep every affected model item blocked until this Gate closes. ### Mandatory list Report and export Gate Before discovering or selecting a Report capability, settle its observable product invariants and record the applicable technical contracts below. An unresolved business result, permission, amount meaning, or state remains a `business_blocker`; unspecified reversible mechanics use the requirements decision routing above and do not become product questions. Delivery and acceptance must still prove every applicable contract: 1. **List Report pagination:** every list Report has bounded server pagination: platform standard or `page_size` plus opaque cursor, maximum page size from the platform contract or a recorded safe default of 200, stable ordering with a deterministic unique cursor tie-breaker, explicit `truncated`, and `total_semantics` of `exact` or `at_least`. Page maximum and tie-breaker are `safe_implementation_decision` items when they do not change an accepted business ordering rule. A transport page that materializes the complete result before slicing is not bounded execution. 2. **Same-Report threshold routing:** export prepare makes one bounded probe of the same Report under normalized parameters and current authorization/data Scope. The fixed threshold is 1000: an exhausted `0..1000` probe yields the exact total and one synchronous governed CSV; observing row 1001 immediately routes to the platform asynchronous paged export-job substrate, whose terminal result records the final exact total. Both branches use the identical Report/SQL/source hash/parameters/Scope; no count-only or export-only second query is allowed. 3. **Asynchronous reauthorization and terminal notification:** before asynchronous page one, the worker reconstructs the current persisted project user-role principal in the frozen workspace and compares canonical authorization Scope, failing closed on real drift. It never substitutes a manifest-only role or synthetic Surface. Only this branch publishes requester-only `completed`/`failed` Inbox notifications linked through export job, audit, and artifact. 4. **Atomic fingerprint replay:** the server canonicalizes Report key, normalized parameters, SQL/source hash, requester/workspace, authorization/data-Scope hash, format, and result version. Equivalent requests atomically reuse an accepted/running job or a completed unexpired artifact without a second file, download record, or terminal notification. `audit_id` stays out of the fingerprint; only failed/cancelled work or expired/corrupt artifacts may create one new execution through database compare-and-create. Require `pagination_trace`, a signed cursor strategy, and `query_profile` evidence captured on the current managed Runtime database cohort: SQLite uses `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN`, MySQL uses `EXPLAIN FORMAT=JSON`, and PostgreSQL uses `EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON)`. Bind the evidence dialect to the managed process receipt's `database_driver`; never provision a second engine only for profiling or fall back to SQLite. Preserve statement/row-count budgets and structured index/full-scan classification. Read [capabilities/reports.md](capabilities/reports.md) whenever a page/API returns Report rows or offers Report export. If the delivery cannot prove the contracts, classify the in-scope Report list/export as `acceptance_failed` with a Runtime Report owner gap. Never substitute browser-memory pagination, repeated full-result execution per chunk, generic batch download, duplicate artifacts, a second query, invented infrastructure, or excluded scope. Before capability selection or model authoring, read [production-technical-gates.md](production-technical-gates.md) completely and derive G01-G32 applicability from the current requirements/model demand pool. # Backend model files

`backend/model/*.json` is the backend metadata inventory and source of truth; `backend/reports/*.sql` is the source-owned SQL surface referenced by Report model items. The Blueprint Ledger under `domain/` and everything under `.domainry/` are CLI-owned projections that `model apply` converges from those sources. Never edit `domain/**`, rendered Blueprints, or `.domainry/**` by hand, and never treat them as an authoring input.

## File contract

Every file under `backend/model/` matching `*.json` is loaded, in lexical filename order:

```json
{
  "contract_version": "domainry-backend-model-v1",
  "items": [
    {
      "module": "project",
      "kind": "project",
      "key": "project",
      "payload": {"blueprint": {"schema_version": "1", "id": "gym", "name": "Gym", "description": "Gym operations"}}
    },
    {
      "module": "membership",
      "kind": "actor_role",
      "key": "membership-roles",
      "requirement_keys": ["membership-management"],
      "depends_on": ["project/project/project"],
      "payload": {"emits": []}
    }
  ]
}
```

Item fields:

- `module`, `kind`, `key` — required identity. `kind` is one of `project`, `requirement`, `actor_role`, `object_relation`, `action_authorization`, `workflow_connector`, `acceptance`, `resource`. Identity segments are stable lowercase keys; the unique project item is always `project/project/project`.
- `status` — optional, `closed` (default) or `decision_required`; `decision_required` must match at least one unresolved decision.
- `requirement_keys`, `depends_on`, `decisions` — optional arrays (default empty). `depends_on` entries are full `module/kind/key` addresses.
- `payload` — the item body (default `{}`), identical to the Ledger item payload contract for that kind.

One `module/kind/key` may be declared exactly once across all model files. Group items by owning module — typically one file per module (`backend/model/<module>.json`). Do not add envelope fields (`contract_version`, `module`, `kind`, `key`) inside `payload`, and do not nest `status`, `requirement_keys`, `depends_on`, or `decisions` there.

## Requirement payload

A `requirement` item's `payload.requirement` carries the requirement statement plus its `behaviors[]` array of behavior-owner tuples (owner, resource_key, and the tuple fields defined in [behavior owner decision](capabilities/behavior-owner-decision.md)). An empty `behaviors` array is legal only when the payload also supplies a non-empty `no_executable_behavior_reason` string explaining why the requirement owns no executable behavior (for example, purely declarative authorization/navigation policy carried by roles, data permissions, and views). The field must be absent when `behaviors` is non-empty; `model validate` fails closed on both violations (`empty behaviors require a reason` / `ledger.requirement_incomplete`).

For `object_sql_v1`, use exactly one project-owned SQL file named after the Report key instead of embedding a large escaped SQL string. Replace only the `sql` member with `"sql_file":"backend/reports/<report-key>.sql"`. `model validate|plan|apply` requires that exact canonical project-relative regular file, rejects symlinks/traversal and simultaneous `sql` + `sql_file`, normalizes line endings and a final newline, records its SHA-256 in the apply receipt, and embeds the normalized SQL into the existing published Runtime contract. `sql_file` is not a Runtime field or a query DSL; Runtime still receives `object_sql_v1.sql`, and `model export` may therefore emit the compatible inline form.

## Commands

```text
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model preflight --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model validate --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model plan     --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model apply    --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --go-module-path <domain-qualified-module> [--environment <name> | --service <url>] [--allow-destructive] [--sync-only] [--evolution-audit-sha256 <emitted-sha256> --evolution-reason <reviewed-reason>]
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model export   --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" [--force]
```

- `preflight` is the authoritative no-HTTP, local-read-only repair loop. It reuses the same model/SQL loader, strict item contract, Ledger graph, in-process authoring checks, and deterministic Runtime-manifest compiler as the formal path. It atomically replaces `.domainry/builder/disposable/model-preflight-result.json` for both `valid` and `repair_required`; stdout contains only `state`, `issue_count`, the project-relative artifact locator, SHA-256, and identity. A repair result exits non-zero. Read the artifact from the first Gate run and batch-repair it; do not rerun a failed Gate merely to obtain diagnostics and do not implement a bespoke `jq`/regex preflight. This local boundary does not claim live Plane, Runtime configuration, provider, database, or scenario checks.
- `validate` parses every model file, enforces the item contract, and reports the pending plan counts without writing model/Ledger state.
- `plan` additionally lists the exact item IDs classified as create, update, or delete.
- `apply` is the single release command: it converges the Ledger to the model files, gates on the aggregated metadata checklist, then chains live validation, signed publication, dependency resolution, backend materialization/evolution, and source finalization, stopping at the first failing stage. Every release apply resolves the dependency seed in staging before it installs files or writes a successful materialization receipt; a resolution failure stops closed and must be repaired before rerunning. For an existing Builder delivery change, the first run emits `evolution_review_required` plus an audit path and SHA-256. Inspect the immutable audit and rerun the same command with that exact emitted SHA-256 and a concrete review reason; never calculate or substitute the hash. After any other failure, repair the model files (or the reported stage input) and re-run the same command. stdout carries one compact summary; the complete receipt is written to `.domainry/builder/model-apply.json`. `--sync-only` stops after the Ledger sync and checklist for local iteration without a Domainry Plane target.
- `export` bootstraps model files from the current Ledger (one file per module) for a project created before this workflow; it refuses to overwrite existing model files without `--force`.

CAS identities, batch contexts, and Ledger journals are handled entirely inside the CLI. Never compute, copy, or supply a SHA-256 by hand, and never call Domainry Plane directly or reconstruct its request signing.

## Convergence and safety rules

`plan`/`apply` classify every declared item against the current Ledger:

- **create / update** — applied automatically and atomically; an unchanged item is never rewritten.
- **delete** — an item present in the Ledger but absent from the model is destructive. `apply` refuses and names the missing items until the model restores them or the run explicitly passes `--allow-destructive`.
- A **rename** of `module`, `kind`, or `key` is a delete plus a create. Treat renames as destructive: confirm data expectations first, then apply with explicit consent.
- The model owns definitions only. Runtime instance data — business records, sessions, credentials, user-role assignments made at runtime — is never compared or mutated by convergence.

Complete each module's full inventory (Objects, Relations, Actions, Roles, authorization, data scopes, Workflows, state machines, Reports, Schedulers, Automations, Connectors, seeds, acceptance) before the first `model validate`; do not validate a partial inventory and do not use `validate` or `apply` as a resource-by-resource schema probe. Immediately before the first validation, perform one cross-resource preflight over the whole draft: ownership closes **both ways** (every requirement behavior resolves to its resource, and every emitted Action/Workflow/Scheduler/Automation — including export/audit helper Actions — has one matching behavior owner); every Action's allowed roles have the required object access plus reads of every declared project relation target; Identity bootstrap/demo-user/profile references resolve; every frontend entrypoint object exists; Report SQL paths equal `backend/reports/<report-key>.sql`; export controls resolve their Report, Action, audit/download Objects, mappings, and one role's complete grant chain; every declared Object has a valid seed; and acceptance actors, roles, operations, positive cases, and denial cases resolve. Run validation only after this inventory is closed. On failure, collect and repair the complete diagnostic set and re-run once; do not revalidate after each local edit. Once validation returns `state:"valid"`, keep that model immutable while attaching evidence. Any requirement-backed edit invalidates the result and starts a new atomic `validate` + `plan` cycle. After a failed apply, fix the complete finding set in the files and re-run once.

**Initial/default-state closure is part of that single preflight.** For every explicit requirement or accepted evidence statement that names an initial or default field value, author the value as the owning `objects[].fields[].default_value`. This is mandatory when the Object is exposed through generic Runtime create (including `entrypoints[].create_objects` or a role's `<object>.create` permission); acceptance prose, a seed, a frontend form default, or an Action input constant is not metadata default behavior. Mechanically verify that every select default matches its stable field option vocabulary and every state-field default matches both that vocabulary and the owning `state_machines[].states`. If the requirement does not identify an initial/default value, do not invent one merely to satisfy prose; record only the deterministic behavior the accepted demand actually establishes.

Before that first validation, apply this strict nested-shape card; these objects reject aliases and convenient prose fields:

- `identity_bootstrap.menus[]` uses `id`, `key`, `label`, optional `description`/`route`/`icon`/`parent_id`, and required `sort_order` plus `status`; there is no `surface`. Bind roles with one row per pair, `role_menus:[{"role_id":"technician","menu_id":"menu_my_work"}]`, or with `role_menu_sets:[{"role_id":"technician","menu_ids":["menu_my_work"]}]`; never use `role_key`, `menu_keys`, or a grouped object under `role_menus`.
- Object field `validation` uses the exact Blueprint keys `min_length`, `max_length`, `min`, `max`, `pattern`, `options`, and `target`; `minimum`/`maximum` are Runtime authoring API names, not Blueprint JSON fields.
- Every `expected_reports[].metrics` value is an array; use `[]` when the scenario asserts execution/export but no metric values. It is never an object map.
- A Report emission repeats its identity inside the value: `{"collection":"reports","key":"part_usage_report","value":{"key":"part_usage_report",...}}`. The envelope `key` does not populate `value.key`; omitting the inner key makes `sql_file` resolve against an empty report key. The two keys must be identical.
- For `object_sql_v1`, each SQL `JOIN ... AS <alias>` has exactly one `join_cardinalities` entry shaped `{"alias":"<alias>","cardinality":"many_to_one"}` (or another truthful supported cardinality). It has only `alias` and `cardinality`; never use `left_alias`/`right_alias` there. Those names belong to Dataset join definitions, not Object SQL cardinality declarations.
- `report_export_controls[]` is closed to the fields listed in [reports](capabilities/reports.md). Do not invent requester/scope convenience properties; requester scoping is enforced by the declared grant chain and record mapping.
- `object_sql_v1` SQL has explicit `ORDER BY` and a literal business-bounded `LIMIT` in the inclusive range `1..10000`; the Blueprint `limit` diagnostic refers to SQL text, not a JSON `limit` property. Never use a larger placeholder such as `LIMIT 100000`.

Business menu definitions and role-menu assignments are **not emitted collections**. They are deterministic project bootstrap facts under the single project-level `identity_bootstrap` object. When acceptance names `effective_menu_list`, declare the needed `identity_bootstrap.menus` and either `role_menus` or `role_menu_sets` before apply; authoring rejects a probed role with no binding. Do not postpone that acceptance prerequisite to a manual post-apply step. Runtime's Identity menu management API remains the supported path for later operational edits; updates keep their normal schema-hash CAS contract.

`identity_bootstrap` (departments, organization scopes/memberships, workforce profiles/assignments, menus and role-menu bindings) is **not** an emits collection — an emitted collection always renders as an array and fails `schema.type: expected object`. It is a single project-level Blueprint property: declare it inside the **project item's `payload.blueprint.identity_bootstrap`** as `{"version":"1","departments":[{"id":"east","name":"East"}],"menus":[{"id":"menu_my_work","key":"my_work","label":"My work","route":"business.my_work","sort_order":10,"status":"active"}],"role_menus":[{"role_id":"technician","menu_id":"menu_my_work"}]}`. `version` is the **string** constant `"1"` (integer `1` fails `schema.const`). `demo_users[].department_id` must reference a department `id` declared there (`identity.user_department_not_found` otherwise).

`demo_users[].profile_bindings` is the single owner of a demo user's business-profile link. Its referenced profile seed must leave the profile extension's `identity_relation_field` absent; do not also write a user ID into that seed field. `model validate` rejects the two-owner form as `identity.user_profile_seed_relation_owned_twice`, before Runtime bootstrap. Runtime still converges the exact pre-existing same-user link idempotently for older valid deliveries, but a different-user replacement remains a conflict.

Two more Action/role rules the validator enforces:

- **Every project-owned Handler Action — including scheduler-driven bulk handlers — must declare at least one required payload field in `idempotency_keys`** (`ledger.action_idempotency_required`). A scheduled job's invocation payload carries the key (e.g. a required `run_date` bound from the trigger event).
- **Multiple `data_permissions[]` entries for the same object do NOT merge**: the validator reads one entry's `read`/`write` per object, so "read=department + write=own" cannot be expressed as two entries (`ledger.action_role_data_permission_required` reports the losing entry's booleans). Declare a single entry with the union capability and enforce the narrower write constraint through a before-update automation assert on the owner, a Handler precondition, or CRUD permission removal.

## Single ownership

Every rendered resource key has exactly one originating model item. A `ledger.resource_duplicate` diagnostic means a second item attempted to emit an existing resource; it is never an overlay or merge mechanism. Repair it in the model files: remove the duplicate declaration and extend the item that already owns the resource. For example, a missing permission on an emitted role belongs in the item that already emits the role, not in a new `actor_role` item emitting the same role key.

Every behavior `resource_key` must resolve to the concrete resource owned by that behavior; the exact owner-to-emitted-collection mapping and resource-key rules live in [behavior owner decision](capabilities/behavior-owner-decision.md) — do not guess a collection from prose.

Agent metadata is resource-owned in the same model: emit `skills`, `agents`, `agent_tasks`, `agent_service_principals`, and `agent_entrypoints` from separate `resource` items in dependency order, each linked to the requirement it satisfies. Never place these collections inside the project item. Read [Agents and Agent Tasks](capabilities/agents-and-agent-tasks.md) before authoring them; exact fields and references come from the live Blueprint Definition consumed by `model validate|plan|apply`.

## Action declarations

An emitted `actions[]` entry requires `key`, `name`, `object_key`, `kind`, and `audit_event`. `kind` is the closed enum `bulk_operation`, `conditional_update`, `object_create`, `object_operation`, `record_delete`, `record_operation`, `record_restore`, `record_update`, or `transition_state`.

**Kind selection for Handler Actions**: a project-owned Handler must NOT use kind `object_create` — that kind carries the system `record.create` owner, and an Action with both a system operation and a business handler owner is rejected at **Runtime bootstrap** ("action has both system operation record.create and business handler owners"); no static stage (validate/finalize/check/verify/package) catches it. Use **`object_operation`** for an object-level Handler command (creation included) and **`record_operation`** for a record-targeted one; a Handler that creates records does the create through its data capabilities.

Authorization splits by ownership and both halves are enforced at compile time (`ledger.runtime_manifest_invalid`):

- A **project-owned Handler Action** (one that declares `handler`) uses the `authorization` block (`allowed_roles`, …).
- A **system Action** (`transition_state` and every other non-Handler kind) must instead declare `permission` — it compiles to Runtime `requires_permission`. `authorization` is rejected on a system Action, and a missing `permission` is rejected too. Runtime executes a system Action for any role holding that permission, so a role that must not execute a guarded transition (for example, "only managers close") must not hold the declared permission — or the transition must be owned by a manager-only Handler Action instead.
- **The `permission` key must be exactly two dot-segments: `<object_key>.<suffix>`** (e.g. `ticket.transition_close`, not `ticket.transition.close`). Runtime authorization re-derives the check as `<action.object_key>.<last-segment>`, so a three-segment key like `ticket.transition.start` passes `model validate` and one authorization layer but is re-read as the never-granted `ticket.start` by the second — every legitimate caller then fails with 403 `backend.permission.denied` at runtime. Platform permission keys granted verbatim in `roles[].permissions` (e.g. `identity.audit.view`) are exact-match strings and are not subject to this rule; it binds project-declared Action `permission` values and object CRUD keys.

Acceptance scenarios are strict Blueprint resources, not free-form test notes. Use only the declared top-level fields `key`, `name`, `description`, `actor`, `role`, `role_key`, `seed_data`, `seed_records`, `actions`, `attempted_actions`, `workflows`, `expected_outcome`, `expected_error_code`, `expected_records`, `expected_reports`, `assertions`, and `config`; never invent shortcuts such as `objects` or `attempted_objects`. Express record/RLS expectations through `expected_records` or typed `assertions`.

`workflows` means a positive **manual** Workflow invocation and therefore requires `trigger_contract.type:"manual"`. Do not list `scheduled`, `action_completed`, or `record_event` Workflows there: the finalizer attributes them to their real trigger owner (the matching `scheduled_jobs`, Action, or Automation operation) and rejects a fabricated manual-run case with `acceptance.workflow_manual_trigger_required`.

The scenario-level `expected_outcome` closed enum is `""`, `positive`, `exception`, or `denied` — nothing else. Use `positive` for an expected success, `denied` for an expected Runtime authorization denial, and `exception` for every other expected non-success (state-machine rejection, RLS concealment, business precondition failure). Do not confuse it with the different `config.runtime_operations[].expected_outcome` enum documented below; the two enums are validated independently and values are not interchangeable. A `denied` scenario's role must actually be unable to execute every attempted Action: the composer rejects a denied scenario whose role holds the Action's authorization (`compose.acceptance_denied_role_can_execute_action`) — pick a genuinely unauthorized role or remove the grant.

### Acceptance composition rules enforced by `project acceptance prepare`

The denominator builder enforces these composition rules; authoring scenarios without them costs one repair round each:

- **Requirement coverage**: every `requirement` item — including purely declarative ones such as acceptance provisioning or navigation — must be reachable from at least one `acceptance` item's `requirement_keys` whose scenarios produce executable cases (`acceptance.requirement_coverage_missing: <key> resources=N operations=0 cases=0` otherwise). Cases come only from `actions`/`attempted_actions`, `workflows`, `expected_reports`, and `config.runtime_operations`; a scenario carrying only `expected_records` produces no case.
- **Write denial coverage**: every write operation — each write Action and each write `runtime_operations` route — needs a denied-role case (`acceptance.permission_denial_missing`). For Actions, author a `denied` scenario with an unauthorized role. For typed routes, author a scenario whose `runtime_operations` entry sets **`"case": "permission_denied"`** (setting only `expected_outcome: denied` is not recognized); its default error code is `auth.permission_denied`, and its role must genuinely lack the route's required permissions.
- **Handler positive coverage is symmetric and DIRECT**: every Handler Action also needs a positive scenario whose `actions` list references it directly with an allowed role (`ledger.action_positive_scenario_missing`). Coverage through a Workflow branch that invokes the Handler does not count — a scheduler-driven or approval-driven Handler still needs one direct positive probe (e.g. the operator role invoking it with an explicit payload).
- **Every declared Object needs at least one seed** — including runtime-product objects such as reminder records or export audit/download artifacts (`ledger.seed_evidence_incomplete` names the missing objects); there is no exemption for objects normally populated only at runtime.
- Treat seed records as a closed typed graph before apply: every required field needs a value or declared default, every `$record:<seed-key>` relation must target a seed of the relation's declared object, option values must belong to the field value domain, and undeclared fields are errors. `model validate` reports these at the exact seed field; do not defer them to Runtime bootstrap.
- **Relation-typed `payload_fields` require `target_object_key`** referencing a **project** object; a Foundation target (e.g. an organization unit) is not resolvable there — pass the identifier as `text` and keep the Object field itself as the real relation.
- **Denied report cases are auto-derived — never author them.** A scenario referencing a report in `expected_reports` must use a role that IS allowed to read it (`acceptance.report_role_not_allowed` otherwise). For a protected report (non-empty `audience_roles`/`required_permissions`), the builder automatically finds an unauthorized role and emits the `permission_denied` case itself; it fails `acceptance.report_denied_role_missing` if no declared role is unauthorized. The same auto-derivation applies to Workflow denied cases.
- **CRUD/list/navigation coverage uses `config.runtime_operations` route keys** from the pinned Runtime Domain API `routes` map. The most-used keys: `object_query` (bounded list GET /objects/{objectKey}/records), `object_detail`, `object_create` (idempotency-key required), `object_update`, `object_delete`, `object_action`, `record_action`, `record_export`, `record_import_apply`, `effective_menu_list` (GET /identity/effective-menus), `business_notification_list`/`business_notification_stream` (SSE). Verify a key's readiness through `contract capability-category` before relying on it.
- **Prepare prerequisites**: a current verification receipt, a running healthy managed Runtime of the exact current cohort, and the runtime-client SDK materialized. Pass `--project` as an **absolute path** — a relative path currently fails the database-identity check with `managed Runtime database identity escapes the current project`.

Their nested shapes are closed too. `expected_records[]` accepts only `object_key`, `record_key`, `field_key`, `state`, `count`, and `values`; it has no `scope`. `expected_reports[]` accepts only `report_key`, `expected_run`, `expected_export`, `filters`, and array-valued `metrics` (use `[]`, not `{}`, when no metric is asserted). Assertions accept only their published typed assertion fields.

When a requirement consumes a typed Runtime capability that is not already represented by `actions`, `workflows`, or `expected_reports`, declare it under the scenario's `config.runtime_operations`. Each entry uses only `route_key` from the pinned Runtime Domain API plus optional `case`, `lifecycle`, `restart_sensitive`, `expected_outcome`, and `expected_error_code`; unknown fields, wrong field types, and route keys absent from the pinned Runtime Domain API fail during `model validate` (`evidence.typed_operation_route_unknown`). Use separate positive and `permission_denied` scenarios/roles for a write. The acceptance denominator resolves the route to the unified capability disclosure, preserves its real read/write effect class, required permissions, and SSE disposition, and rejects an allowed role labeled denied, a positive role missing the published permission, or a write without both positive and denied coverage. `expected_outcome`, when supplied, is one of `passed`, `denied`, `conflict`, `rejected`, `concealed`, `not_found`, or `failed`. For an SSE route, the case/lifecycle must be `sse_disconnect_resume`/`disconnect_resume` and `restart_sensitive` must be omitted or `false`: Last-Event-ID reconnect is not a managed process restart and requires only the stream transcript plus durable refetch. Do not reduce it to a connection-open check or attach unrelated restart/audit evidence.

```json
{"config": {
  "runtime_operations": [
    {"route_key":"business_notification_stream","case":"sse_disconnect_resume","lifecycle":"disconnect_resume"}
  ]
}}
```

A positive scenario's referenced seed records must already satisfy every source-owned Handler precondition needed for the expected success path. Every positive or denied role used by executable acceptance must have a project-declared `demo_users[]` identity. Bind a specific identity through `actor`; when an automatic standard case only has a role, that role must have exactly one demo user or exactly one user marked `acceptance_default:true`. The default applies across both `role_key` and `role_keys`; alphabetical order is never identity resolution. A role label alone is not a login. Keep separate negative business-precondition scenarios when that rejection matters. Denied authorization scenarios remain distinct and must fail at the Runtime authorization boundary.

When a positive Action needs a value the standard runner cannot derive, declare the runner-owned fixture in that scenario's open `config` map: `"action_payloads":[{"action_key":"<declared scenario action>","fields":{"<payload key>":{"value":<typed scalar>}}}]`. An omitted `encoding` requires a literal conforming exactly to the declared scalar payload type; relation/reference literals accept only `$record:<seed-key>` of the declared target, and user literals accept only `$actor`. The existing `{"encoding":"json","value":<array or object>}` form remains available only for `text`/`long_text`, resolving nested `$record:<seed-key>` values before canonical JSON encoding. The Action must belong to that positive scenario, actor plus Action must identify one scenario/role binding, and malformed, missing-seed, duplicate, or ambiguous fixtures fail closed; fixture fields are never conflict-mutation slots. Do not declare fixtures for values the standard type derivation already supplies.

Validation must close actor/role, object/relation, Action/authorization/data access, Automation/Workflow/Scheduler ownership, frontend entrypoints, and positive plus denied acceptance. Single-owner semantics and behavior shape tuples live in [behavior owner decision](capabilities/behavior-owner-decision.md).
